title: A Hybrid Retrieval Approach for Advancing Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 7th International Conference on Natural Language and Speech Processing (ICNLSP 2024)
actual_contribution: Hybrid retrieval combining dense text embeddings with knowledge graph embeddings can improve retrieval accuracy and ranking for domain-specific RAG | Knowledge-graph-augmented retrieval captures inter-passage global relationships that pure text embeddings miss, supporting better evidence selection
limitation_or_note: Evaluation is on a small proprietary health-tech dataset with LLM-generated synthetic queries; no robustness, noise, or adversarial evidence analysis.
human_supports_claims: Hybrid retrieval combining dense text embeddings with knowledge graph embeddings can improve retrieval accuracy and ranking for domain-specific RAG | Knowledge-graph-augmented retrieval captures inter-passage global relationships that pure text embeddings miss, supporting better evidence selection
human_rationale: The paper proposes a hybrid retriever that fuses fine-tuned BGE text embeddings with translational KG embeddings (TransE/RotatE/QuatE) to better capture global passage relations in a health-tech QA use case, and reports modest improvements in HitRate, MRR, and end-to-end answer correctness across several LLM readers. It is relevant to the evidence-construction perspective for KG-augmented retrieval but does not directly study unreliable evidence, noise, conflict, or abstention. Workshop venue with small custom test sets and a single proprietary domain limit its evidential weight, so appendix placement under extended evidence-construction coverage is appropriate.
human_caveat: Evaluation is on a small proprietary health-tech dataset with LLM-generated synthetic queries; no robustness, noise, or adversarial evidence analysis.
map_b_adjudication_notes: Paper proposes a hybrid text+KG retrieval method to improve retrieval accuracy in a health-tech RAG application; only briefly mentions 'false retrieval' as motivation without principled analysis or mitigation of evidence reliability, distraction, conflict, adversarial, or calibration issues, so it is a general RAG improvement rather than a robust-RAG contribution.

title: Accelerating Inference of Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Sparse Context Selection
authors: Yun Zhu; Jia-Chen Gu; Caitlin Sikora; Ho Ko; Yinxiao Liu; Chu-Cheng Lin; Lei Shu; Liangchen Luo; Lei Meng; Bang Liu; Jindong Chen
actual_contribution: Self-assessment via special control tokens can filter irrelevant retrieved contexts within a single model pass, improving generation quality while reducing latency. | Sparse context selection acts as an internal corrective mechanism, offering an alternative to external classifiers like CRAG for handling noisy retrieved evidence.
limitation_or_note: Efficiency is the primary contribution; robustness to unreliable evidence is a side benefit and is evaluated only on standard QA/summarization datasets without adversarial or counterfactual noise.
human_supports_claims: Self-assessment via special control tokens can filter irrelevant retrieved contexts within a single model pass, improving generation quality while reducing latency. | Sparse context selection acts as an internal corrective mechanism, offering an alternative to external classifiers like CRAG for handling noisy retrieved evidence.
human_rationale: The paper proposes Sparse RAG, which encodes documents in parallel and uses learned control tokens to assess per-context relevance, then selectively decodes attending only to high-relevance KV caches. While the primary motivation is inference acceleration, the per-context assessment mechanism is directly relevant to filtering unreliable/noisy evidence, and the paper explicitly compares against Self-RAG and CRAG as robustness baselines. Placement in appendix is appropriate because the central contribution is efficiency rather than robustness, though the unified self-assessment design is a useful data point for evidence-filtering lineage. Overclaim risk: it should not be cited as a robustness-focused method since reliability is a byproduct rather than the explicit goal.
human_caveat: Efficiency is the primary contribution; robustness to unreliable evidence is a side benefit and is evaluated only on standard QA/summarization datasets without adversarial or counterfactual noise.
map_b_adjudication_notes: Both coders independently identify this as efficiency-focused sparse context selection for inference acceleration, with no threat model, calibration, or robustness benchmark; the incidental filtering of irrelevant docs is a side effect of latency optimization, so boundary/exclude is appropriate.

human_caveat: Does not explicitly evaluate robustness to noisy, conflicting, or poisoned passages; gains are demonstrated on standard multi-hop QA and document reasoning benchmarks.

actual_contribution: KG-grounded RAG can improve faithfulness by distilling structural priors (relation paths) into LLMs via SFT plus KTO preference optimization. | Constraint-based introspection with backtracking is a viable action-control mechanism for verifying reasoning paths and triggering retries when retrieved evidence violates question constraints.
limitation_or_note: Constraints are predefined manually and the evaluation is limited to three KGQA benchmarks, so generalization to truly noisy or adversarial retrieval is not directly demonstrated.
human_supports_claims: KG-grounded RAG can improve faithfulness by distilling structural priors (relation paths) into LLMs via SFT plus KTO preference optimization. | Constraint-based introspection with backtracking is a viable action-control mechanism for verifying reasoning paths and triggering retries when retrieved evidence violates question constraints.
human_rationale: The paper proposes DP, a KG-RAG framework that combines progressive knowledge distillation for faithful relation-path generation with a reasoning-introspection module that extracts predefined constraints, verifies whether candidate reasoning paths satisfy them, and backtracks when they do not. This is directly relevant to robust RAG under unreliable evidence in the graph/KG scenario, illustrating both evidence construction (path planning/instantiation) and action control (constraint verification, feedback-driven backtracking). Case-study placement in the modality section is appropriate because it is a specific KG-RAG method rather than a general robustness mechanism, and overclaiming should be avoided since constraints are still partly hand-defined.
human_caveat: Constraints are predefined manually and the evaluation is limited to three KGQA benchmarks, so generalization to truly noisy or adversarial retrieval is not directly demonstrated.
map_b_adjudication_notes: Both coders correctly identify this as a KG-RAG accuracy method using structural priors and introspection for faithful reasoning, not a robust-RAG-under-unreliable-evidence contribution; canonical's graph_kg scenario tag does not by itself confer scope without an evidence-reliability robustness mechanism.

actual_contribution: KG community-level retrieval can address sparse and semantically misleading retrieval in traditional RAG for high-stakes domains like clinical prediction. | Combining structured KG retrieval with multitask fine-tuning enables interpretable reasoning chains alongside predictions in domain-specific RAG. | Multi-source KG construction (biomedical KG, corpus, LLM-derived triples) improves contextual relevance compared to naive dense retrieval.

human_supports_claims: KG community-level retrieval can address sparse and semantically misleading retrieval in traditional RAG for high-stakes domains like clinical prediction. | Combining structured KG retrieval with multitask fine-tuning enables interpretable reasoning chains alongside predictions in domain-specific RAG. | Multi-source KG construction (biomedical KG, corpus, LLM-derived triples) improves contextual relevance compared to naive dense retrieval.
human_rationale: KARE integrates hierarchical KG community detection with LLM reasoning for EHR-based mortality and readmission prediction, explicitly framing the work as addressing the limitations of traditional RAG that retrieves semantically similar but clinically irrelevant information. For a survey on robust RAG under unreliable evidence, it serves as a representative case study of graph/KG-based evidence construction in a biomedical scenario, with concrete ablations isolating retrieval components (node hits, coherence, theme relevance). Overclaim risk: gains are largely from domain knowledge structuring, not directly from adversarial or noisy-evidence robustness.
human_caveat: Evaluation is limited to MIMIC datasets and two clinical prediction tasks, and the framework does not directly address adversarial or poisoned evidence.
map_b_adjudication_notes: Domain-specific healthcare KG-RAG framework (KARE) for mortality/readmission prediction on MIMIC; the core contribution is KG construction plus community retrieval for accuracy, not analysis/mitigation of unreliable evidence, conflicts, attacks, or calibration, so it is out of scope for the robust RAG map.

human_supports_claims: RAG can reduce hallucination in structured output generation by grounding the LLM in retrieved schema-valid items (steps and table names) | A small fine-tuned retriever paired with a moderately sized LLM can match or exceed a much larger LLM without retrieval, including in out-of-distribution settings
human_rationale: The paper is an industrial case study showing that RAG over JSON step and table indices reduces hallucinated entities (from up to 21 percent down to under 7.5 percent) in a workflow generation task and improves OOD generalization. It is relevant to a robust-RAG survey as a domain-specific structured-output scenario where evidence quality and retriever recall directly determine output validity. Case-study placement fits because it is application-focused and does not propose new mechanisms for evidence reliability, conflict, or abstention beyond grounding in retrieved candidates. Overclaim risk: the paper measures only one proprietary task and acknowledges residual hallucination even with RAG.
human_caveat: Proprietary enterprise data and metrics; conclusions on retriever-LLM trade-offs may not generalize beyond JSON workflow generation.
map_b_adjudication_notes: Both coders correctly identify this as an industry application paper deploying RAG for structured JSON workflow generation without an evidence-reliability robustness mechanism; falls under scope exclusion for domain-specific RAG applications.

human_supports_claims: MuRAG extends retrieval-augmented generation to multimodal memory by jointly indexing images and text, enabling answers to visual information-seeking queries that text-only RAG cannot address. | Joint contrastive and generative pre-training over image-text and text-only corpora improves both retrieval and grounded generation in multimodal QA. | Error analysis reveals shortcut learning where the model relies on textual clues rather than visual grounding, highlighting a robustness/faithfulness gap in multimodal RAG.

limitation_or_note: Noise robustness is demonstrated via accuracy on standard benchmarks rather than dedicated unreliable-evidence stress tests, and the approach is specific to graph-structured retrieval rather than general RAG.
human_supports_claims: Retrieval-augmented generation can be extended to graph learning by constructing a toy-graph vector library and injecting retrieved subgraph features and labels through message-passing prompts. | Noise-aware prompt tuning with deliberately retrieved irrelevant or bottom-K subgraphs improves robustness against noisy retrieval in graph RAG. | Inverse importance sampling helps surface long-tail knowledge in the graph retrieval base, mitigating bias toward high-degree nodes.

map_b_adjudication_notes: RAGraph applies retrieval-augmentation to GNNs for cross-task graph generalization without addressing evidence reliability, conflicts, adversarial corruption, calibration, or robust RAG evaluation; both coders correctly flag it as out of scope.
